source.title: Going Deeper With Directly-Trained Larger Spiking Neural Networks
source.authors: Hanle Zheng; Yujie Wu; Lei Deng; Yifan Hu; Guoqi Li

record.file_problem: The complete paper text, including supplementary material, is present. Some figure-axis labels are garbled, but the surrounding text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly trains spiking neural networks from scratch on CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and neuromorphic datasets, extending deep-network training results to a different model class. Its reported classification metrics are test accuracy, not training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-set accuracy and gradient-norm analyses, but no training classification error or training-loss result. Its CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and shortcut-related accuracy results do not establish whether the claim's predicted training error is reached. The cited ResNet, normalization, initialization, and related methods are prior work, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study adapts batch normalization and residual shortcuts to train spiking networks and reports its method's test accuracy and gradient propagation. It does not measure any version's specified training-error effect, initialization comparison, training-speed advantage, or learning-rate stability behavior.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that tdBN balances neuronal inputs and thresholds and alleviates gradient propagation problems; combined with modified residual shortcuts, it enables directly trained deep SNNs with high classification accuracy and few inference timesteps. These conclusions do not establish the training-error, speed, or learning-rate comparisons specified by the claim versions.
record.recipe_differences: Directly trains spiking neural networks with STBP-tdBN and modified residual shortcuts; reports test accuracy and gradient-norm behavior rather than training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Gradient-norm curves vary with τdecay (0, 0.25, 0.5); the text says τdecay=0 prevents temporal information propagation and causes serious degradation. Dataset, architecture, and timestep settings also vary across reported accuracy evaluations.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 20-layer plain SNN with tdBN, gradient norms during the first sixth of an epoch are steady at membrane decay 0 and increase slowly across layers at decay 0.25 and 0.5 (Figure 2). There is no normalization-free control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Threshold-dependent batch normalization can maintain approximately stable gradient magnitudes across layers in a plain spiking network.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed residual SNNs achieve high held-out classification accuracy, including 67.05% on ImageNet with a widened ResNet-34 and 64.88% with ResNet-50, both using six timesteps (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: STBP-tdBN with modified residual shortcuts enables direct training of deep spiking networks with competitive held-out accuracy and few inference timesteps.

record.peer_reviewed: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (copyright notice); paper text does not state a venue for this version.
record.problems: No training classification error or training loss is reported, so the paper's accuracy results do not answer the claim's training-error criterion. Dataset accuracy comparisons mostly cite other models; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Gradient-norm evidence is shown in figures and described in text, but is not a direct measurement of training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: accuracy results are test-set performance and the gradient-norm analysis does not measure the training-error behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: No training classification error, CIFAR-100 experiment, or corrupted/random-label experiment is reported.
No ReLU teacher-student problem, spurious-local-minimum frequency, or extra-student-neuron comparison.
No training-error comparison across depths or between plain and residual networks. Higher ImageNet test accuracy for ResNet-50 than ResNet-34 does not establish prevention of training degradation.

No comparison of activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth. The tdBN gradient analysis does not test those effects.
No comparison with an initial stability threshold, loss-rise-and-recovery trajectory, sharpness trajectory, or divergence boundary.
No matched normalization-versus-no-normalization comparison of training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and no Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification should be corrected to uses_without_test/T4. Its empty eligible-row set is appropriate, and rows_left_out already declares the omitted test-accuracy and gradient-norm results. Few inference timesteps measure inference latency, not faster optimization.

versions.untested_parts: No training classification error is reported; CIFAR-10 accuracy is test accuracy. No CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random-label experiment.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum rate, or student-width sweep.

The paper uses residual SNNs and analyzes gradients in a 20-layer plain SNN, but does not report plain-versus-shortcut training classification error or compare training error by depth. Its dataset accuracy results are test accuracy.
The study proposes tdBN and analyzes gradient norms, but does not compare the initialization methods specified in the version or report training-error outcomes.
No learning-rate stability-limit or sharpness experiment.
The paper uses tdBN for SNNs, but does not compare batch normalization against no normalization on training speed or learning-rate tolerance as stated in this version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
